question: How do the phonemes ra and la emerge from the same will-power?
premises: The same will-power can quickly take on the stain of the knowable.
It can incline toward a different power.
Different modes of this inclination yield different phonemic forms.
inference: The phonemes ra and la are further transformations of the will-power as it engages otherness and the knowable.
uncertainties: The text does not explicitly distinguish which condition yields ra versus la.
plain_english: That same power, quickly taking on the stain of the knowable and turning toward another, becomes ra and la.
